title: Bridgeport housing rezoning approved with traffic concerns
subtitle: Parkland acquisition strategy, farmers market fee cuts, SAP procurement, Kitchener Green subdivision, heritage designations and Oktoberfest noise exemption.
overview: Council approved a rezoning and vacant land condominium for 26 Stanley Avenue and 31 Schweitzer Street in Bridgeport {{vote:m1}}. Amendments limit homes backing onto Schweitzer Street to two storeys and bar raised rear balconies. Council also directed staff to write to the Region of Waterloo about traffic congestion and access in the neighbourhood. Nearby residents had asked for a deferral over traffic, water and sewer capacity, and emergency access.

Council endorsed a Parkland Acquisition Strategy that focuses on King East, Bridgeport West and the KW Hospital area {{vote:m15}}. It approved fee reductions and delegated authority for vendors at the Kitchener Farmers Market, which is operating under an interim model after a fire {{vote:m16}}. It also approved a rezoning and subdivision changes for Kitchener Green {{vote:m13}}, non-standard procurement with SAP Canada for ERP modernization {{vote:m17}}, a heritage designation notice for 87 Margaret Avenue {{vote:m3}}, and a noise exemption for Oktoberfest events {{vote:m6}}.
The Mayor reported that the city's tariff and trade task force has resumed work to support local businesses, and gave an update on water allocation for housing projects.

decisions.detail: Council approved the zoning amendment and vacant land condominium, with added limits on height and rear balconies for homes backing onto Schweitzer Street, and directed a letter to the Region about Bridgeport traffic {{vote:m1}}.
Council approved the zoning amendment and major modifications to two draft plans of subdivision, using revised conditions for one plan from the addendum report {{vote:m13}}.
Council endorsed the strategy and its key actions, which prioritize land for parks in King East, Bridgeport West and the KW Hospital area {{vote:m15}}.
Council approved vendor fee reductions and delegated authority to staff to set temporary rates until normal operations return {{vote:m16}}.
Council approved non-standard procurement to negotiate and enter into agreements with SAP Canada {{vote:m17}}.
Council directed the Clerk to publish a Notice of Intention to Designate the property under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m3}}.
Council granted K-W Oktoberfest Inc. an exemption from the noise bylaw for events at various locations from September 25 to October 17, 2026 {{vote:m6}}.

debate: Two delegates opposed the Stanley Avenue and Schweitzer Street proposal and asked for a deferral. They cited strain on the aging watermain and sewer, traffic around the Lancaster and Bridge Street area, emergency response access, and a cemetery pathway still shown on the draft plan.

The applicant's consultant said the site already has height permissions and objected to new limits on height or second-storey balconies. The consultant said the intent is traditional two-storey homes.

Staff said the cemetery connection will not be pursued and fencing will be required. They said the traffic study was accepted by the City and Region, and the added units are a small increase over what the zoning already allows. They noted a refusal could be appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, which could remove the concessions.
Councillors said they were not satisfied with the Region's response on Bridgeport traffic and that the City cannot fix it through this application. That led to the added letter to the Region.

On parkland, one councillor questioned why budget review was set for 2027 rather than this year. Staff said existing parkland trust funds can cover the three priority areas, and that other funding options would be considered later.
